newsitem.title: GERMANY: Apple - Q3 sales up q/q in parts of Europe.
newsitem.headline: Apple - Q3 sales up q/q in parts of Europe.

text.p: Troubled Apple Computer Inc said on Thursday third-quarter sales in units and revenue rose slightly from the second quarter in certain European countries .
Sales in Germany and France increased from the second quarter but fell from fiscal 1996's third quarter, Apple spokeswoman Therese Wermelskirchen told Reuters.
In Britain, unit sales and revenue rose versus the last quarter and year ago levels. Apple's third quarter ended June 28.

"Overall (in Europe), the third quarter of 1997 was less than the third quarter of 1996," she said. "But we are seeing encouraging signs in Italy, Spain and the Middle East, and in Norway and Scandanavia."
She said growth was less than the industry average but declined to give specific figures. Instead, she said "we are coming out of a very weak situation in the last 18 months."
Apple's European results compare with Compaq Computer Corp's 41-percent jump in unit terms and 21-percent increase in dollar terms in the quarter ended June 30. Compaq reported earnings last week.
Apple plans to release the next version of its operating system, Mac OS 8, in Europe in September and give free upgrades to customers who buy new Macintosh computers before then, she said.
Mac OS 8 is due to debut next week in the United States.

Wermelskirchen said she saw no effect so far from chief executive officer Gilbert Amelio's unexpected resignation last week. Amelio had been called in 17 months ago to return the once-leading computer maker to profitability.

On Wednesday, Apple reported a third-uarter loss of $56 million as worldwide sales slumped year-on-year 23 percent to $1.7 billion. On a quarterly basis, sales rose slightly from the second quarter's $1.6 billion.
